p0.original: 关键问题：意识每天会发生怎样的周期循环
p0.en: Key issue: How the cycle of awareness happens every day

p2.original: 意识的周期性波动与我们的生物节律和环境中的刺激模式相对应。
p2.en: The cyclical fluctuations in consciousness correspond to the stimuli in our biological rhythm and environment.

p3.original: 如果你喜欢早起，你可能在刚刚醒来时就处于最警觉的状态，但这种精神状态不会持续一整天。像大多数其他人一样，你可能会在下午经历一段无精打采的时间，此时你可能会像拉丁世界的大多数人一样，明智地午睡一会儿。之后，你的警觉性会在一段时间内得到提升，但在傍晚时分会再次降低。高度集中注意的时间以及被称作白日梦的遐想时间可能会时不时地打断这个周期。但无论你是一个“喜欢早起”的人还是一个“夜猫子”，最终你的意识都会几乎停止与外界接触，进入占据你生命中三分之一时间的睡眠状态。
p3.en: If you like to get up early, you might wake up in the most alert state of mind, but that state of mind will not last all day. Like most other people, you may experience an insinuation in the afternoon, when you may be as wise as most people in the Latin world to take a nap. After that, your vigilance will be raised over time, but it will be reduced again in the evening. The time of intense concentration and thoughttime, known as the daydream, may break the cycle from time to time. But whether you're a "like to get up early" or a "night cat," you end up in almost no contact with the outside world, into a state of sleep that takes up one third of your life.

p4.original: 心理学家考查了意识的这些周期性变化，并找寻这些周期性变化中的可靠模式。这一部分的核心概念总结了他们已有的发现。
p4.en: Psychologists examined these cyclical changes in consciousness and looked for reliable patterns of these cyclical changes. The core concepts of this section summarize what they have found.

p5.original: 意识的周期性波动与我们的生物节律和环境中的刺激模式相对应。
p5.en: The cyclical fluctuations in consciousness correspond to the stimuli in our biological rhythm and environment.

p6.original: 在这一部分中，我们主要关注睡眠和夜间做梦涉及的意识的周期性变化。不过，我们先从清醒时发生的另一种“梦”开始。
p6.en: In this section, we focus primarily on the cyclical changes in consciousness involved in sleep and nighttime dreams. But let's start with another dream that happens when we're sober.

p8.original: 8.4 描述白日梦的出现频率和价值。
p8.en: 8.4 Describe the frequency and value of the occurrence of daydreams.

p10.original: 8.6 评价梦的内容、其与现实生活的相关性、产生的原因、生理机能和作用。
p10.en: 8.6 Evaluate the content of dreams, their relevance to real life, the causes, physiological functions and effects.

p13.original: 描述白日梦的出现频率和价值。
p13.en: Describe the frequency and value of the daydream.

p14.original: 在我们称之为白日梦（daydreaming）的状态中，意识发生了轻微的改变，注意转向了内部的记忆、期望和欲望，这通常会伴有生动的心理表象（Roche & McConkey，1990）。当人们独自一人、轻松自在、做无聊或常规的任务、困意十足时，白日梦最常出现在人们的大脑中（Singer，1966，1975）。但是做白日梦正常吗？其实大多数人每天都会做白日梦，知道这一点可能会令你感到宽慰。事实上，如果你不做白日梦，反而是不正常的！平均而言，我们大约有30%醒着的时间都在做白日梦，其中年轻人的白日梦最频繁、最生动。随着年龄的增长，白日梦的发生频率和强度似乎都在显著下降（Giambra，2000；Singer & McCraven，1961）。
p14.en: In what we call the daydreaming state, there has been a slight change in consciousness and attention has shifted to internal memories, expectations and desires, which are usually accompanied by vivid psychological appearances (Roche & McConkey, 1990). When people are alone, comfortable, do boring or routine tasks, and are so desperate, daydreams are most frequently found in people's minds (Singer, 1966, 1975). But is daydream normal? Most people actually have daydreams every day, and knowing that might comfort you. In fact, if you don't have a daydream, it's not normal! On average, about 30 per cent of our awakenings are in daytime dreams, of which young people have the most frequent and vivid dreams. With age, the frequency and intensity of daydreams seem to be decreasing significantly (Giambra, 2000); Singer & McCraven, 1961.

p15.original: 8.4.1 我们为什么会做白日梦

p16.original: 玛丽亚·梅森及其同事（Malia Mason et al.，2007）的一项脑扫描研究表明，做白日梦可能是不可避免的事。当我们的大脑处于静息状态，不专注于外部任务时，一个被称为“大脑默认网络”的区域就会接手。这是一个集中于颞叶和额叶区域的复杂网络，其“默认”活动被认为是一种持续不断的向内聚焦的加工倾向，特别关注我们的经验如何与我们现在的生活以及过去和未来的生活相关。进化心理学家认为这一默认网络可能是具有适应性的，因为它会让我们在某种意义上保持对重要事物的觉知（即使我们没有注意到）。当人们幻想未来，回忆他们的过去或者想象某人的感受或想法时，这一网络的活动似乎是最强的（Buckner et al.，2008）。因此，即使在休息时，大脑也是兴奋的、保持活跃的，这一发现将有助于我们理解稍后将介绍的夜间的梦。
p16.en: A brain scan study by Maria Mason et al. and her colleagues (Malia Mason et al., 2007) shows that daydreaming may be inevitable. When our brain is in a static state and is not focused on outside tasks, a region called the Brain Default Network will take over. This is a complex network focused on the region of the leaf and the forehead, whose “default” activity is considered to be a continuous, inward-focused processing trend, with particular attention to how our experience relates to our lives now, as well as to past and future lives. Evolutionary psychologists believe that this default network may be adaptive, because it would allow us to maintain, in a sense, a sense of awareness of important things (even if we do not notice them). This network seems to be the strongest activity when people imagine the future, remember their past, or imagine someone's feelings or ideas (Buckner et al., 2008). So, even at rest, the brain is excited and active, a discovery that will help us understand the night dreams that will be introduced later.

p17.en: 8.4.2 Whether daydreams are beneficial or harmful

p18.original: 白日梦可以为宝贵的健康功能服务（Klinger，1987）。我们在白日梦里通常想的是我们生活中的实际问题和当前关注的问题，如课程、目标（无关紧要的或至关重要的）和人际关系。当我们思索这些问题时，白日梦可以针对这些问题制订计划并提出解决方案：对某些人来说，这种白日梦增加了实现其目标的机会（Langens，2003）。白日梦还是创造性洞察力的源泉，就像直觉（intuition）的闪现。当面对一个难题时，偶尔的走神可以使我们的大脑进入无意识联想，可能会产生揭示完美解决方案的“啊哈”瞬间（Schooler et al.，1995）。
p18.en: Daydreams can serve valuable health functions (Klinger, 1987). What we normally think in our daydreams is the real problems and current concerns in our lives, such as curricula, goals (irrespective or vital) and interpersonal relations. When we think about these issues, daydreams can plan and propose solutions to them: for some, they increase opportunities to achieve their goals (Langens, 2003). Daydreams are also a source of creative insight, like the flash of intuition. When faced with a dilemma, occasional distractions can bring our brain into unconscious association, and may produce “aah-ha” moments that reveal perfect solutions (Schooler et al., 1995).

p19.original: 做白日梦是一种正常的人类活动，有助于创造力的迸发和问题解决。不过研究表明，当我们全神贯注于一项任务时是最快乐的，所以做白日梦的时机影响它是否有益于你的健康。
p19.en: Daydreaming is a normal human activity that contributes to creativity and problem resolution. But research shows that when we focus on a mission, we are the happiest, so the timing of a daydream affects whether it is good for your health.

p20.original: 不过，要注意选择做白日梦的时间。最新的研究表明，做白日梦会干扰对最近学习材料的记忆。并且白日梦距离现实越远，这种效应就越大：做出国度假的白日梦的学生相较于做在当地度假的白日梦的学生，忘记了更多最近学习的内容（Delaney et al.，2010）。这表明，如果你在一个重要的学习过程中陷入白日梦，那么你就有可能忘记刚刚学习的一些内容。
p20.en: However, care should be taken to choose the time of daydreaming. Recent studies have shown that daydreaming interferes with the memory of recent learning materials. And the further away from reality, the greater the effect: students on national holidays forget more about their recent studies than students on local holidays (Delaney et al., 2010). This suggests that if you get into a daydream in an important learning process, then you may forget something you just learned.

p21.original: 我们还必须对做白日梦提出另一条警告。来自哈佛实验室的马修·基林斯沃思（Matthew Killingsworth）和丹·吉尔伯特（Dan Gilbert）的一项研究威胁到了我们对白日梦最常见的假设之一——做白日梦是在追求快乐这一观念（Killingsworth & Gilbert，2010）。
p21.en: We must also give another warning to the daydream. A study by Matthew Killingsworth and Dan Gilbert from Harvard Laboratories threatens one of the most common hypotheses of day-to-day dreams — the idea that day-to-day dreams are seeking happiness (Killingsworth & Gilbert, 2010).

p22.original: 一项针对2000多名所有年龄段的成年人的研究使用了专门开发的iPhone应用程序，以便在一天中的任意时间对被试进行调查。当他们的应用程序响铃时，被试会回答几个关于他们正在做什么、他们是否专注于此以及他们有多快乐的简短问题。
p22.en: A study targeting more than 2,000 adults of all ages used a specially developed iPhone application to investigate the trial at any time of the day. When their applications ring the bell, they are tried to answer a few brief questions about what they are doing, whether they are focused on it and how happy they are.

p23.original: 研究结果揭示了一些可能会让你感到惊讶的事情。你认为人们什么时候最快乐？
p23.en: The results reveal something that might surprise you. When do you think people are the happiest?

p24.original: 人们全神贯注地沉浸于一个任务时最快乐，而非做白日梦时。因此，尽管走神可能是我们脑内线路系统的一部分，但似乎专注的人更快乐。
p24.en: People are so enthralled in the happiest of a mission, not in daytime dreams. So, while detached may be part of our internal circuit system, people who seem focused are happier.

p25.original: 白日梦与晚上的梦相比如何呢？不管我们的幻想多么逼真，白日梦都很少像我们大多数丰富多彩的夜间梦境那样生动。它们也没那么神秘——因为它们更容易被我们控制。它们的发生也不会像夜间梦境一样，受生物周期和我们称之为睡眠的陌生世界的影响。现在我们就将注意力转向这个夜间的世界。
p25.en: How about a daydream compared to a nightdream? No matter how real our fantasy may be, daydreams are rarely as lively as most of our rich night dreams. And they're not so mysterious -- because they're easier for us to control. They will not happen in the same way as nighttime dreams, affected by biological cycles and by what we call a strange world of sleep. Now we turn our attention to this night world.

p26.original: 8.5 睡眠：我们生命中神秘的三分之一
p26.en: 8.5 Sleep: A third of our lives are mysterious.

p29.original: 如果你活到90岁，那么你的睡眠时间就有将近30年。但这种神秘的精神状态是什么？睡眠的世界曾经是精神分析学家、先知、诗人和画家的领地，现在则是一个充满活力的科学研究领域。科学研究表明，睡眠是我们的自然生物周期之一（Beardsley，1996）。我们以对这些周期的考察，来开启对这一改变了的意识的领域的探索。
p29.en: If you live to be 90, you'll sleep for almost 30 years. But what is this mysterious state of mind? The world of sleep, once the domain of psychoanalysts, prophets, poets and painters, is now a dynamic field of scientific research. Scientific research has shown that sleep is one of our natural life cycles (Beardsley, 1996). By examining these cycles, we begin to explore the areas of this changed consciousness.

p31.original: 所有生物都会受到自然周期变化的影响，尤其是每天的明暗交替模式。其中，对人类最重要的是昼夜节律（circdian rhythms），即大约每24小时重复一次的身体模式［英文中“昼夜”（circadion）一词源于拉丁语中意为“大约”和“一天”的circa和dies］。对这些周期节律进行内部控制的是我们的下丘脑（hypothalamus），在下丘脑，我们的“生物钟”设定了如新陈代谢、心率、体温和激素活动等机能的节律（Pinel，2005）。下丘脑中被称作视交叉上核（Suprachiasmatic Nucleus，SCN）的细胞群接受来自眼睛输入的信息，因此，它对白天和黑夜的明暗循环特别敏感（Barinaga，2002）。所以，从生物学角度来看，睡眠和觉醒的交替循环只是另一种昼夜节律。
p31.en: All organisms are affected by natural cycle changes, especially the dark and dark alternation patterns that occur every day. Of these, the most important for humanity is the day and night rhythm (circdian rhythms), i.e. the body pattern, which is repeated approximately every 24 hours [the word “circadion” in English], which is derived from the Latin meaning of “approximately” and “one day” Circa and dieies]. Internal control of these cycles is our hypothalamus, where our “biological clock” sets the rhythms of function such as metabolism, heart rate, body temperature and hormone activity (Pinel, 2005). The cells in the sub-crop, known as the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus, SCN, receive information from eye input and are therefore particularly sensitive to the dark cycle of day and night (Barinaga, 2002). So from a biological point of view, the alternation of sleep and awakening is just another day and night rhythm.

p32.original: 对大多数人来说，我们正常的睡眠-觉醒模式在自然条件下会比一天略长。在没有时间线索的环境中长期生活时，大多数人都会进入近25小时的昼夜节律周期。然而，在一个24小时的世界中，我们会通过每天暴露在阳光下的时间和习惯性的日常活动来重新调整我们的模式（Dement & Vaughan，1999）。
p32.en: For most people, our normal sleep-awakening pattern is slightly longer than a day under natural conditions. In the absence of a time trail, most people enter a round-the-clock cycle of almost 25 hours. However, in a 24-hour world, we will re-engineer our model by the time and customary routines that are exposed to sunlight every day (Dement & Vaughan, 1999).

p33.original: 昼夜节律影响旅行者（和其他所有人） 我们的自然昼夜节律周期的时间跨度略长于24小时，这可以解释时差反应，其症状包括疲劳、不可抗拒的瞌睡和暂时的认知缺陷。当我们向西飞行时，我们的身体会相对容易地适应当地更长的白天，因为白天的延长与我们更长周期的自然趋势相吻合。例如，你从纽约飞达西雅图时是晚上7点，你处于纽约时间的身体认为现在是晚上10点。在这种情况下，大多数人可以晚睡一会儿以适应新的时区，并在第二天早晨在适当的当地时间醒来，而不会受到昼夜节律的影响。然而，向东飞行则是另一番景象了，因为你会失去几个小时。早晨7点的闹铃（当你的身体认为现在是凌晨4点时）可能是一种粗鲁的唤醒，你将难以正常工作。因此，在你的昼夜节律周期中减少数小时会比增加数小时产生更大的时差反应——每减少一小时，你的身体可能会需要大约一天来恢复。出于这个原因，专家推荐了多种策略来帮助你在实际到达当地的前几天就开始适应当地时间。
p33.en: The day and night rhythms affect travellers (and all others) our natural day and night cycle spans slightly longer than 24 hours, which can explain the time differential response, with symptoms of fatigue, irresistible slumber and temporary cognitive deficiencies. As we fly west, our bodies will adapt relatively easily to the longer day in the area, because the longer day is consistent with the natural trend of our longer cycles. For example, you flew from New York to Seattle at 7 p.m. and your body in New York time thought it was now 10 p.m. In such cases, most people can sleep late to adapt to the new time zone and wake up at the appropriate local time the next morning, without being affected by the day and night. However, heading east is another picture, because you'll lose hours. The alarm at 7 a.m. (when your body thinks it's 4 a.m.) may be a rude wake-up call, and you will have difficulty working properly. So, a few hours less in your day and night cycle would have a much greater time differential reaction than an additional hours — every hour less, your body might take about one day to recover. For this reason, the experts have recommended a variety of strategies to help you adapt to local times a few days before you actually arrived.

p35.original: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，睡眠都是一个谜，直到1952年的一个深夜，研究生尤金·阿瑟瑞斯基（Eugene Aserinsky）决定记录他正在睡觉的儿子的脑电波和眼睛的肌肉运动（Brown，2003）。记录顺利地进行了大约一个半小时，在脑电图（EEG）上记录到的只是缓慢的睡眠节律。然后，一连串的眼动突然间出现了。记录显示，男孩的眼球来回转动，仿佛在观看快速变化的场景。与此同时，脑电波模式显示男孩是警觉的。阿瑟瑞斯基以为儿子已醒来并在环顾四周，但当他走进卧室时，却惊讶地发现儿子仍在熟睡，闭着眼睛静静地躺着。出于好奇，研究人员在更多的志愿者身上重复了相同的程序，并在所有人身上都发现了相似的模式。
p35.en: For most of human history, sleep was a mystery until a late night in 1952, when a graduate student, Eugene Aserinsky, decided to record his sleeping son's brainwaves and eye muscle movements (Brown, 2003). The records were smooth for about an hour and a half, and only slow sleep rhythms were recorded on the EEG. And then, suddenly, a series of eye moves appeared. The records show that the boy's eyeballs are turning around as if he were watching a fast-changing scene. At the same time, the brain wave pattern shows that boys are alert. Aserreski thought that his son had woken up and looked around, but when he entered the bedroom, he was surprised to find his son still asleep and lying silently with his eyes closed. Out of curiosity, researchers repeated the same procedures on more volunteers and found similar patterns in everyone.

p36.original: 在睡眠期间，我们大约每隔90分钟就会进入阿瑟瑞斯基所发现的那种状态。我们现在称它为快速眼动（Rapid Eye Movement，REM）睡眠，其以快速脑电波和闭合眼睑下的快速眼球运动为特征，这种状态会持续几分钟或更长时间，然后再突然停止（Aserinsky & Kleitman，1953）。没有快速眼动的过渡期被称为非快速眼动（non-REM，NREM）睡眠。
p36.en: During our sleep, we enter the state of Aschersky about every 90 minutes. We now call it Rapid Eye Movement, which is characterized by rapid brain waves and fast eyeball motion under closed eyelids, which lasts for a few minutes or more and then suddenly ceases (Aserinsky & Kleitman, 1953). The transition period without rapid eye movement is called non-fatal eye movement (non-rem, Nrem).

p37.original: 在这两个不同的睡眠阶段，心理上和大脑中会发生什么？为了查明这一点，研究人员在快速眼动睡眠或非快速眼动睡眠期间唤醒睡眠者，要求他们描述自己的心理活动（Dement & Kleitman，1957；McNamara et al.，2005）。非快速眼动时的报告通常包含对普通日常事件的简要描述或根本没有心理活动。相比之下，快速眼动时的报告则充满了生动的认知，以奇异怪诞的场景为特征，而且带有攻击性质。换句话说，快速眼动是做梦的标志。
p37.en: What happens psychologically and in the brain at these two different stages of sleep? In order to identify this, researchers awakened sleepers during fast eye contact or non-fast eye contact sleep and asked them to describe their psychological activities (Dement & Kleitman, 1957); McNamara et al., 2005. Reports that do not move quickly often contain a brief description of ordinary routine events or no psychological activity at all. By contrast, reports of rapid eye movement are full of vivid knowledge, characterized by strange scenes and of an aggressive nature. In other words, rapid eye movement is the hallmark of a dream.

p38.original: 令人奇怪的是，当眼球在快速眼动睡眠期间转动时，身体其他部位的随意肌却保持不动，这种情形被称为睡眠性麻痹（sleep paralysis）。从进化的角度来看，这可能会阻止我们的祖先在做梦时游荡至洞穴之外并陷入麻烦。（顺带一提：梦游和说梦话不会发生在快速眼动睡眠期间，而是发生在非快速眼动睡眠的更深层的阶段。）我们随后会讲述更多关于梦的内容。现在，让我们来看看快速眼动睡眠是如何与其他睡眠阶段配合工作的。
p38.en: It is strange that while the eyeballs move during fast eye motion sleep, the random muscles of other parts of the body remain intact, a situation known as sleep palalysis. From an evolutionary point of view, this may prevent our ancestors from wandering beyond the caves and getting into trouble in their dreams. (Appendix: Sleepwalking and talking do not take place during fast eye contact sleep, but at a more advanced stage of non-fast eye contact. We'll talk more about the dream. Now, let's see how fast eye motion sleep works with other sleep stages.

p40.original: 想象你是一个有关睡眠实验的被试。在与脑电图（EEG）记录设备相连接后，你适应了连在身体上的设备，并安顿下来小睡了一晚。随着睡眠周期的进行，你的脑电波会发生怎样的变化？第二天早晨仔细观察这一周期的记录，你会发现几个不同的阶段（见图8-5），每个阶段都有一个典型的EEG信号。
p40.en: Imagine you're an experiment on sleep. After being connected to the EEG recording device, you adapted to the physical device and settled down for one night. How does your brain wave change as the sleep cycle unfolds? Looking closely at the record of the cycle the next morning, you will find several different stages (see figure 8-5), each with a typical EEG signal.

p41.original: 图8-5 各睡眠阶段的EEG模式
p41.en: Figure 8-5 EEG patterns for sleep periods

p42.original: 在一个普通夜晚的睡眠中，大多数人都会经历4～6个睡眠周期，每个周期又包含数个睡眠阶段。在每个接下来的周期中，深度睡眠（第三和第四阶段）的时间都会减少，而快速眼动睡眠的时间会增加。因此，我们可能会在完整的睡眠时间结束时，获得长达一小时的快速眼动睡眠。看一下图8-6，它向你展示了在典型的夜间睡眠中表现出来的模式。
p42.en: In a normal night sleep, most people go through four to six sleep cycles, each of which includes several sleep stages. In each subsequent cycle, the time of deep sleep (phases 3 and 4) is reduced, while the time of fast eye contact sleep is increased. So we may get a quick eye mover sleep for up to an hour at the end of the full sleep time. Take a look at figure 8-6, which shows you the pattern of typical night sleep.

p44.original: 你的睡眠是什么样的呢

p45.original: 在回顾图8-6中的信息后，请考虑一下你自己的睡眠模式。根据你每晚的平均睡眠时间，你的深度睡眠时间大约是多少？快速眼动睡眠时间呢？你的答案与每晚约8.5小时的平均睡眠需求相比如何？
p45.en: After reviewing the information in figures 8-6, please consider your own sleep patterns. What's your average sleep time per night? What about fast eye contact? What's your answer to the average sleep requirement of about 8.5 hours per night?

p46.original: 请注意正常睡眠的三个最重要的特征：
p46.en: Please note the three most important features of normal sleep:

p48.original: （2）在夜幕降临不久后发生最深度的睡眠；
p48.en: (2) The deepest sleep occurs shortly after the nightfall;

p49.original: （3）随着睡眠的进行，快速眼动持续时间增加。
p49.en: (3) Rapid eye motion increases with sleep.

p51.original: 注：在一个典型的夜晚，最深度的睡眠（第三和第四阶段）主要发生在最初的几小时里。随着夜色加深，睡眠者会在第三和第四阶段花费更少的时间，而在快速眼动睡眠中花费更多的时间。
p51.en: Note: At a typical night, the deepest sleep (phases III and IV) takes place mainly in the first few hours. As the night becomes darker, sleepers spend less time in the third and fourth phases, and more time in fast eye sleep.

p52.original: 如果一个人被剥夺了整晚的快速眼动睡眠会发生什么情况呢？你怎么看？
p52.en: What happens if a man is deprived of a fast eye sleep all night? What do you think?

p53.original: 实验室研究会通过在睡眠者每次进入快速眼动睡眠时唤醒他们来研究快速眼动睡眠剥夺。第二天，被剥夺快速眼动睡眠的睡眠者会表现出疲倦和易怒程度的增加。然后，在接下来的晚上，他们通常会延长快速眼动睡眠，这种情况被称为快速眼动反弹（REM rebound）。这一观察表明快速眼动睡眠满足了某种生理需求。请睡眠不足的大学生注意：因为我们大部分的快速眼动睡眠是在晚上最后的几个周期里进行的，所以如果我们没能在晚上睡个好觉，那么我们就会不可避免地受到快速眼动睡眠剥夺和快速眼动反弹的折磨。
p53.en: Laboratory research is conducted to study rapid eye motion sleep deprivation by awakening sleepers every time they enter fast eye motion sleep. The next day, sleepers deprived of rapid eye sleep showed increased fatigue and anger. Then, in the following night, they usually prolong the fast eye motion sleep, which is called the rapid eye motion rebound (REM response). This observation shows that rapid eye motion sleep meets a physical need. Attention of underslept students: Because most of our fast eye sleep takes place in the last few cycles of the night, if we do not get a good night's sleep, we will inevitably suffer from fast eye sleep deprivation and fast eye bounce.

p55.original: 睡眠在动物中如此普遍，因此它肯定具有某些基本功能，睡眠科学家提出了几种可能性（Maquet，2001；Rechtschaffen，1998）。进化心理学认为，睡眠的进化可能是为了使动物在无须觅食或寻求配偶的时候保存能量及远离伤害（Dement & Vaughan，1999；Miller，2007）。此时，这些功能就由大脑的生物钟来协调。
p55.en: Sleep is so widespread in animals that it certainly has certain basic functions, and sleep scientists have suggested several possibilities (Maquet, 2001); Rechtschaffen, 1998. Evolution psychology believes that the evolution of sleep may be designed to preserve energy and distance animals from harm when there is no need to feed or to seek a spouse (Dement & Vaughan, 1999; Miller, 2007. At this point, these functions are coordinated by the biological clocks of the brain.

p56.original: 几个世纪前，威廉·莎士比亚（William Shakespeare）谈到“睡眠会把忧虑的乱丝编织起来”，诗意地描述了睡眠的另一个功能。因此，他推测，睡眠可能对身心都具有修复功能。现在的研究表明，这确实是真的：在第三和第四阶段，我们最深度的睡眠期间，身体和大脑中受损的细胞将得到修复，生长激素得以释放，使这些阶段成为免疫系统恢复的关键时期，以及再生和加强因日常磨损而受损的肌肉和组织的关键时期。快速眼动睡眠可以帮助大脑清除一天中积累的不想要的无用信息——就像清空你的垃圾桶一样（Crick & Mitchison，1983）。实验还表明，快速眼动睡眠可以改善认知功能，尤其是记忆力、创造力和问题解决能力（Wagner et al.，2004）。而睡眠剥夺会抑制这些过程（Siegel，2003；Winerman，2006b）。虽然在洞悉睡眠如何使我们恢复活力的方面已经取得了一些进展，但睡眠科学家仍未获知睡眠的全貌（Winerman，2006b）。
p56.en: A few centuries ago, William Shakespeare spoke of “sleep woven the wiring of worry”, a poetic description of another function of sleep. He therefore assumes that sleep may have a prosthetic function both physically and mentally. Current research shows that this is true: during the third and fourth phases of our deepest sleep, damaged cells in our body and brain will be repaired, growth hormones released, making these stages critical to the recovery of the immune system, as well as to the regeneration and reinforcement of muscles and tissues damaged by daily wear and tear. Rapid eye-sleep helps the brain to remove unwanted and useless information accumulated in the day - just like emptying your trash can (Crick & Mitchon, 1983). Experiments also show that rapid eye motion sleep improves cognitive functions, especially memory, creativity and problem resolution (Wagner et al., 2004). Sleep deprivation inhibits these processes (Siegel, 2003); Winerman, 2006b. While some progress has been made in understanding how sleep revives us, sleep scientists are still not informed of the full extent of sleep (Winerman, 2006b).

p58.original: 从发展的角度来看，我们的睡眠模式在我们的一生中会有所变化（见图8-7）。
p58.en: From a development perspective, our sleep patterns change over our lifetimes (see figures 8-7).

p59.original: 图8-7 人类在一生中不同阶段的睡眠模式
p59.en: Figure 8-7. Human sleep patterns at different stages of life

p60.original: 虽然我们人体的生理机能和昼夜节律决定了我们的平均睡眠需求，但请记住，不同个体对睡眠的需求可能会有所不同（Barinaga，1997；Haimov & Lavie，1996）。例如，锻炼会影响我们的睡眠需求：若我们在日常生活中进行了剧烈的体力活动，我们就会延长第四阶段的深度睡眠时间（Horne，1988）。
p60.en: While the physical function of our body and the rhythm of day and night determine our average sleep needs, remember that the need for sleep may differ from one individual to another (Barinaga, 1997); Haimov & Lavie, 1996. For example, exercise affects our sleep needs: if we perform intense physical activity in our daily lives, we will prolong the fourth phase of deep sleep (Horne, 1988).

p62.original: 分析与年龄相关的睡眠变化

p63.original: 研究一下图8-7，然后考虑以下问题。
p63.en: Study figures 8-7 and then consider the following questions.

p64.original: 1. 你认为，为什么儿童从出生到3岁会睡得那么多？
p64.en: 1. Why do you think children sleep so much from birth until they reach the age of three?

p65.original: 2. 你认为，为什么平均睡眠时间会在整个生命周期内持续下降？
p65.en: 2. Why, in your opinion, do average sleep times continue to decline throughout the life cycle?

p66.en: 8.5.6 Sleeping debt can cause great trouble

p67.original: 你的母亲是正确的：大多数成年人都需要睡大约8小时，或者更多一点，才能感觉良好并高效工作。在睡眠实验室中，当志愿者置身于一个黑暗的房间中，并被允许进行不受干扰和不参考时间的睡眠时，一般成年人都会进入每晚睡眠时间约为8.5小时的模式。然而，大多数美国人的睡眠时间夜复一夜地显著减少（Greer，2004b；Maas，1999）。这造成了睡眠不足，研究人员威廉·德门特（William Dement）将其称为睡眠债（sleep debt，Dement & Vaughan，1999）。
p67.en: Your mother is right: most adults need to sleep for about eight hours, or a little more, to feel good and work efficiently. In the sleep laboratory, when volunteers are in a dark room and are allowed to sleep without interference or time, adults generally enter a pattern of about 8.5 hours of sleep per night. However, most Americans have significantly reduced their sleep time night after night (Greer, 2004b); Maas, 1999. This resulted in a lack of sleep, which the researcher William Dement described as sleeping debt (sleep debt, Dement & Vaughan, 1999).

p68.original: 长期累积睡眠债的人通常不会意识到这一点（Dement，2000；Dement & Vaughan，1999）。当闹钟在早晨唤醒他时，他可能会昏昏沉沉，但却没有意识到这是睡眠债的迹象，因为他的生物钟会在接下来的几小时内让他进入清醒状态。午后犯困可能被归因于吃了一顿丰盛的午餐，但实际上午餐并不会让人犯困（这又是生物钟）。他也可能通过告诉自己犯困是对无聊的正常反应，来合理化自己在会议中或课堂上为保持清醒而做的挣扎（Van Dongen et al.，2003）。但事实上，对无聊的正常反应是坐立不安，而非犯困（除非一个人睡眠不足）。
p68.en: People who have accumulated sleeping debts for a long time do not usually realize this (Dement, 2000); Dement & Vaughan, 1999. When the alarm wakes him in the morning, he may be fainted, but he does not realize that it is a sign of sleeping debt, because his biological clock will awaken him in the next few hours. The post-morning difficulties may be attributed to a rich lunch, but in practice they do not make people sleepy (which is also a biological clock). He may also rationalize his struggle to stay awake in meetings or classes by telling himself that being trapped is a normal reaction to boredom (Van Dongen et al., 2003). In fact, the normal reaction to boredom is restless, not sleepy (unless a person does not sleep well).

p69.original: 由于昼夜节律，你的生物钟会使你在一天中的某些时刻感到相对警觉，从而出现预定的有规律的觉醒周期（即使你没有足够的睡眠）。但是，如果你有长期的睡眠债，你永远也不会像通过几晚良好的睡眠偿还了睡眠债后那样警觉和高效（Van Dongen et al.，2003）。睡眠债会影响你的生活：睡眠剥夺会导致体重增加，还会导致寿命缩短（National Institute of Medicine，2006）。此外，就像2010年印度的一架客机坠毁事件一样，睡眠债有时会以悲剧的形式得以“偿还”——机上158人全部遇难，飞行员在控制台前睡了将近两个小时，在着陆前才醒过来，而且由于头昏眼花而无法做出正确的判断，飞机冲出了跑道，最终炸成了一团火球（Athrady，2010）。
p69.en: Because of the rhythm of day and night, your biological clock will alert you to certain moments of the day, thus producing a scheduled and regular awakening cycle (even if you do not have enough sleep). But if you had a long sleep debt, you would never be as vigilant and efficient as you were after a few nights of sleep service (Van Dongen et al., 2003). Sleeping debt affects your life: sleep deprivation leads to weight gain and shorter life expectancy (National Insurance of Medicine, 2006). Moreover, like the crash of a passenger plane in India in 2010, sleeping debt is sometimes “repayable” in the form of a tragedy — 158 people were killed on board, the pilot slept in front of the control table for almost two hours, woke up before landing, and the plane ran out of the runway and eventually blew up a ball of fire because of its dazed eyes (Athrady, 2010).

p70.original: 我们应该特别关注的是这个事实：睡眠剥夺对认知和运动功能具有毁灭性的影响（Pilcher & Walters，1997）。根据威廉·德门特的说法，它“让你变得愚蠢”（Dement & Vaughan，1999，p.231）。一项研究刚好展示了它会让人变得多么“愚蠢”，该研究剥夺了一组志愿者的睡眠，并向另一组志愿者提供了足够的酒精，让他们喝到法定的醉酒状态（其血液中酒精的含量达到0.1%）。在24小时未睡后（就像通宵准备考试一样），困倦的志愿者在思维和协调测验中的表现并不比醉酒组好（Fletcher et al.，2003）。你认为在实习医师和住院医师中，如此普遍的长期睡眠剥夺会对医生的表现有什么影响？
p70.en: We should pay particular attention to the fact that sleep deprivation has a devastating impact on cognitive and motor functions (Pilcher & Walters, 1997). According to William Demente, it “makes you stupid” (Dement & Vaughan, 1999, p. 231). A study that just showed how stupid it is to make a person look, deprived a group of volunteers of sleep and provided another group of volunteers with enough alcohol to get them to the state of statutory intoxication (with 0.1 per cent of alcohol in their blood). After 24 hours of sleep (as in the case of the overnight preparation of examinations), tired volunteers do not perform better in their thinking and coordination tests than in drunk groups (Fletcher et al., 2003). How do you think such widespread prolonged sleep deprivation among interns and resident physicians will affect the doctor's performance?

p71.original: 通过回答下面“试一试”版块中附带的问题，查明你是否有足够的睡眠。
p71.en: To find out if you have enough sleep by answering the questions attached to the section below.

p72.original: 应对时差反应和其他昼夜节律变化的技巧
p72.en: Techniques for responding to time differentials and other changes in the rhythm of day and night

p73.original: 每年都有越来越多的人乘坐飞机进行长途旅行（无论是为了工作还是为了娱乐）。不仅狭窄的飞机座位会让所有旅客都不舒服，而且飞越多个时区（特别是从西到东）的旅客还要承受时差反应的影响，其特征是头痛、疲劳、难以集中注意力、失眠，甚至轻度抑郁。一般来说，每跨越一个时区，身体都需要大约一天来调整其时钟。所以，如果你跨越了7～10个时区，却没有有效地应对时差反应，那么你就有可能面对在旅行地刚刚调整好身体，却到了回家的时间的情况！不用说，这会干扰期待已久的度假乐趣或重要的商务旅行的工作效率。幸运的是，对昼夜节律（以及时差如何影响昼夜节律）的基本了解可以提供有关如何减小甚至消除时差反应的技巧。
p73.en: Every year, more and more people travel by air (whether for work or for entertainment). Not only would a narrow aircraft seat be uncomfortable for all passengers, but passengers over multiple time zones (especially from west to east) would also suffer from time differential reactions, characterized by headaches, fatigue, difficulty of concentration, insomnia and even mild depression. Generally, for each time zone to be crossed, the body takes about one day to adjust its clock. So if you cross seven to ten time zones without responding effectively to time differentials, you may face the fact that you've just made a physical adjustment in the travel area and you've come home! Needless to say, it interferes with the long-awaited pleasure of vacation or the efficiency of work on important business trips. Fortunately, basic knowledge of the day and night rhythms (and how time differentials affect the day and night rhythms) can provide techniques on how to reduce or even eliminate the time differential reactions.

p74.original: 1. 调整你的睡觉时间和起床时间，让其更接近目的地时区，如在出发前的几天里逐日增加0.5～1小时。所以，如果你的目的地时区早于你家的时区，那么你就可以越来越早地起床和睡觉；相反，如果你的目的地时区晚于你家的时区，那么你就可以每天更晚一会儿起床和睡觉。这将开始重置你的生物钟，这样当你到达时，时差感就不会那么强烈了。
p74.en: 1. Adjust your sleeping and getting up time to bring it closer to the time zone of destination, for example by adding 0.5 to 1 hour each day in the days preceding departure. So if your destination is earlier than your home, you can get up and sleep sooner; On the contrary, if your destination is later than your home, you can get up and sleep later every day. This will begin to reset your biological clock so that when you arrive, the time difference will not be so strong.

p75.original: 2. 在你办理好登机手续后，立即重置你的电子钟和电子设备以与目的地的时间相吻合，并开始按照这一时间“生活”，仿佛那是正确的时间一样。在航班起飞后保持清醒，直至到了你期望在目的地上床睡觉的时间，然后尝试入睡。穿舒适的衣服，带上毛毯或外套保暖，这将有助于你快速入睡。许多旅行者都会在飞机上使用睡眠眼罩来阻挡光线，这会进一步帮助你的大脑认为现在是夜间。
p75.en: After you have completed the boarding formalities, your electronic clock and electronic equipment will be reset to coincide with the time of destination and will start to “live” at that time as if that was the right time. Stay awake after the flight leaves until the time when you expect to go to bed at your destination and then try to go to sleep. Put on comfortable clothes and take a blanket or a coat to keep you warm, which will help you sleep fast. Many travelers use sleep masks on planes to block light, which will further help your brain think it's nighttime.

p76.original: 3. 为了有助于在飞机上睡觉，饮食要清淡且健康。记住，当你睡觉的时候你会脱水，而航空旅行会使你进一步脱水。因此，要在用餐时喝水或果汁，并随身携带一瓶水，以便在你“夜晚”睡眠期间喝两口。避免喝酒精饮料和吃咸的食物，它们也会助长脱水。你可能无法在飞机上连续酣睡数小时，但即使是浅睡也能帮助你休息。
p76.en: 3. In order to facilitate sleep on the aircraft, the diet must be light and healthy. Remember, you dehydrate when you sleep, and air travel will dehydrate you further. Therefore, water or juice is to be taken during the meal, and a bottle of water is to be brought with you so that you can have two drinks during your “night” sleep. They also contribute to dehydration by avoiding drinking water and salty foods. You may not be able to sleep on the plane for hours, but even a nap can help you rest.

p77.original: 4. 一旦到达目的地，你就要遵守当地的时间表。如果在白天到达，你要忍住小睡的冲动。为了克服时差反应，你能做的最重要的事情就是保持全天忙碌，即使你很疲惫。这样，你就更有可能在第一天整晚安睡。待在外面明亮自然的光线下，这会告知你的大脑现在是白天，并帮助你保持清醒。散散步，避免吃可能让你昏昏欲睡的大餐或喝酒精饮料。然后，在新环境中找一个合适的时间上床睡觉，这样第二天早晨醒来后你就很有可能精神焕发，并准备好享受美好时光！
p77.en: 4. Once you have arrived at your destination, you will have to adhere to the local timetable. If you arrive during the day, you'll have to resist the urge to take a nap. The most important thing you can do to overcome time differentials is keep busy all day, even if you're tired. So you're more likely to sleep all night on the first day. Stay outside the bright light of nature, which will tell you that your brain is now in the daytime, and help you stay awake. Take a walk and avoid eating a large meal or drinking a drink that might make you sleepy. Then find the right time to go to bed in the new environment so that you can wake up the next morning and be prepared to enjoy the good times!

p78.original: 即使是不经常乘坐飞机周游世界的人，也会经历类似的昼夜节律改变的影响（通常每周一次）。我们中的大多数人都倾向于在周末熬夜，因为第二天早晨不必起床去上学或工作。但研究表明，周末每晚睡一小时，第二天早晨就会起得更晚，你会以一种让身体感觉自然的方式向前改变你的昼夜节律。然后，当星期一早晨来临的时候，你的闹钟响起，把你从睡梦中叫醒，你的昼夜节律周期的突然变化会导致一种被称为“星期一早晨忧郁症”的情况。
p78.en: Even people who do not travel around the world by air frequently experience the effects of similar changes in the rhythm of day and night (usually once a week). Most of us tend to stay up late on weekends, because the next morning they do not have to get up to school or work. But research shows that one hour at the end of the week, and the next morning, you'll wake up even later, and you'll change your day and night in a way that makes your body feel natural. Then, when Monday morning comes, your alarm bell will ring and wake you up from your sleep, and sudden changes in your rhythm cycles will lead to a situation known as “Monday morning depression”.

p79.original: 睡一整晚是自然的吗？你可能会把睡眠视为一个发生在大约8小时内，从上床的时间到早晨闹钟把你叫醒时的过程。但这种模式在人类历史上出现得相当晚，且主要限于工业化国家的人们。人类的“自然”倾向是以更不固定的模式进行睡眠，无论何时想睡都可以，白天会睡得短一些，晚上会睡得长一些（Bosveld，2007；Warren，2007）。在一些农村地区，人们通常会在半夜醒来花一两小时聊天、玩耍或照看炉火，这恰好表明我们的睡眠-觉醒时间表多么具有可塑性。
p79.en: Is it natural to sleep all night? You may think of sleep as a process that occurs within about eight hours, from the time of bedtime to the morning alarm that wakes you up. However, this pattern has emerged quite late in human history and is mainly confined to people in industrialized countries. The human “natural” tendency is to sleep in a more irregular manner, whenever you want to sleep, shorter in the daytime and longer in the evening (Bosveld, 2007); Warren, 2007. In some rural areas, people usually wake up in the middle of the night for an hour or two to talk, play or look after the fire, which is just how plastic our sleep-awakening schedule is.

p80.original: 然而，任何缩短你的睡眠时间或使你的生物钟偏离其生物节律的事情都会影响你的感受和行为。黑白轮班的工作时间表正因为这种影响而饱受诟病（Dement & Vaughan，1999；Moore-Ede，1993）——尽管像时差反应一样，当轮班时间向后移动时，导致的症状会比向前移动时更糟糕，并且这种影响可能非常巨大。
p80.en: However, anything that shortens your sleep time or diverts your biological clock from its biological rhythm affects your feelings and behavior. The black and white shift schedule of work is suffering from this effect (Dement & Vaughan, 1999; Moore-Ede, 1993) — Although, as with time differential reactions, when shift time moves backwards, the symptoms are worse than when moving forward, and the effects can be very significant.

p81.original: 一项研究发现，轮班的护士在开车上下班时睡着的可能性是定期值班护士的两倍，在工作中与瞌睡有关的事故或失误的风险也会翻倍（Gold et al.，1992）。
p81.en: A study found that shifts of nurses were twice as likely to sleep while driving to and from work as regular duty nurses, and that the risk of accidents or errors related to slumber at work was double (Gold et al., 1992).

p82.original: 通宵准备考试也具有类似的后果。
p82.en: The overnight preparation of the exams has similar consequences.

p83.original: 根据美国国家睡眠基金会的数据，近三分之一的美国工人报告在过去一个月内，至少有一次曾在工作中睡着了。在轮班工人中（除了在医院和空中交通管制部门工作的人员）这一数字会上升至超过50%。
p83.en: According to the National Sleep Foundation of the United States, nearly one third of United States workers reported having fallen asleep at work at least once in the past month. The number of shift workers (except those working in hospitals and air traffic control) would rise to more than 50 per cent.

p84.original: 试一试 你需要多少睡眠
p84.en: Try it. How much sleep do you need?

p85.original: 许多大学生都长期处于睡眠剥夺状态。因为他们的日程中挤满了学习、工作和社交活动，学生可能会说服自己，他们每晚只需要几小时的睡眠。并且事实上，大学生平均每晚只睡大约6.8小时（Hicks，1990）。
p85.en: Many university students have long been deprived of sleep. Because they have a schedule full of studies, work and social events, students may convince themselves that they only need hours of sleep each night. In fact, university students sleep on average only about 6.8 hours at night (Hicks, 1990).

p86.original: 如果你曾在课堂上睡着，那么可能不是因为课程很无聊。
p86.en: If you've been asleep in class, it's probably not because the classes are boring.

p87.original: 睡眠太少真的会让你在课堂上的表现有所不同吗？你怎么认为呢？
p87.en: Is it true that too little sleep will make you behave differently in class? What do you think?

p88.original: 心理学家谢丽尔·斯宾韦伯（Cheryl Spinweber，1990）发现，睡眠不足的本科生成绩低于睡眠充足的本科生。最近的研究还表明，睡眠剥夺会导致体重增加：每晚睡眠少于7小时的人有很高的肥胖率（Harder，2006）。
p88.en: Cheryl Spinweber, a psychologist, found that undersleeping undergraduates had lower undersleeping grades. Recent studies have also shown that sleep deprivation leads to weight gain: people who sleep less than seven hours a night have a high rate of obesity (Harder, 2006).

p89.original: 如何判断你是否需要更多的睡眠呢？请如实地回答以下问题。
p89.en: How do you know if you need more sleep? Please answer the following questions in a factual manner.

p90.original: 1. 你是否经常在课堂上犯困？
p90.en: 1. Do you often suffer from difficulties in the classroom?

p91.en: Did you sleep late on the weekend?

p92.original: 3. 你在无聊的时候通常会犯困吗？
p92.en: 3. Do you usually get sleepy when you're bored?

p93.original: 4. 你是否会经常在看书或看电视时睡着？
p93.en: Do you often fall asleep while reading or watching television?

p94.original: 5. 你通常会在躺下后5分钟之内睡着吗？
p94.en: 5. Do you usually fall asleep within five minutes of lying down?

p95.original: 6. 你早晨醒来时是否会感觉没有休息好？
p95.en: Does it feel good to wake up in the morning?

p96.original: 7. 如果不用闹钟把你从床上叫起来，你会睡过头吗？
p96.en: 7. Would you overslept if you didn't have an alarm clock to wake you up from bed?

p97.original: 你对这些问题的回答是什么（是或否）？
p97.en: What are your answers to these questions (yes or no)?

p98.original: 如果你对这些问题中的任何一个回答“是”，那么你很可能就有睡眠不足的问题。你可能会在学习质量和学习成绩方面付出代价。如果你开车的话，那么你可能还会将你的生命置于危险之中。
p98.en: If you answer “yes” to any of these questions, then you probably have the problem of sleep deprivation. You can pay for the quality of learning and learning achievement. If you drive, you might put your life in danger.

p101.original: 评价梦的内容、其与现实生活的相关性、产生的原因、生理机能和作用。
p101.en: Evaluate the content of the dream, its relevance to real life, the causes, physiological functions and effects.

p102.original: 你生命中的每一个夜晚，都会有一系列令人叹为观止的事件在你的梦里上演。是什么引起了这些荒诞不经的认知奇观呢？如果梦真有什么含义，那么它们到底意味着什么呢？正如我们之前所看到的，现在睡眠科学家已经知道，梦在整个夜晚都会有规律地发生，最常见于快速眼动睡眠期间。他们还知道，大脑的哪些部分控制着梦，尤其是脑干的部分区域。有关这一睡眠阶段最为神秘的问题仍然是我们为什么做梦。
p102.en: Every night of your life, there is an amazing series of events that take place in your dreams. What's causing these ridiculous cognitive wonders? If dreams really mean something, then what exactly do they mean? As we have seen before, sleep scientists now know that dreams occur regularly throughout the night, most often during fast eye contact sleep. They also know which parts of the brain control dreams, especially those parts of brain stem. The most mysterious question about this sleep phase remains why we dream.

p104.original: 数十年来的研究，为揭示我们做梦的内容以及我们日常的经历如何影响我们梦的内容提供了重要见解。我们了解到了什么？这些认识如何与我们自己做梦的经历联系起来？
p104.en: Decades of research have provided important insights into what we dream about and how our daily experiences affect what we dream about. What have we learned? How do these perceptions relate to our own dream experiences?

p105.original: 梦因文化、性别和年龄而异 文化对梦的内容的影响会以各种不同的方式表现出来。
p105.en: Dreams vary according to culture, gender and age, and the influence of culture on the content of dreams can be seen in different ways.

p106.original: 来自西非国家加纳的报告告诉我们，该地区的人做的梦经常以被牛攻击为特征。
p106.en: Reports from the West African country of Ghana tell us that people in the region often dream of being attacked by cattle.

p107.original: 美国人则经常在他们的梦里因自己在公共场所赤身裸体而感到尴尬，即使这样的报告很少出现在有“单薄”着装文化的地区。
p107.en: Americans are often embarrassed in their dreams by their nakedness in public places, even though such reports rarely appear in areas where there is a “slim” dress culture.

p108.original: 相较于欧洲籍美国大学生，墨西哥籍美国大学生的梦里更常出现死亡的画面。这可能是因为在拉美文化里，死亡是他们生活中更重要的一部分。
p108.en: Mexican American university students dream of dying more often than European American students. This may be because death is a more important part of their lives in Latin American culture.

p109.original: 总体来说，跨文化研究为罗莎琳德·卡特赖特（Rosalind Cartwright，1977）的假说提供了支持。该假说认为，梦反映了做梦者重要的生活事件。
p109.en: Overall, intercultural research supports Rosalind Cartwright's hypothesis. The hypothesis is that the dream reflects the important life events of the dreamer.

p110.original: 睡眠科学家还了解到，梦的内容会受年龄和性别的影响。儿童比成年人更可能梦到动物，并且他们梦中的动物更可能是大型的、有威胁的野生动物。相反，大学生梦到的通常是小型动物、宠物和驯化的动物。这可能是因为孩子们感到他们对自己世界的控制力要远小于成年人，因此当他们睡觉时，会看到世界被描绘成更恐怖的画面（Van de Castle，1983，1994）。
p110.en: Sleep scientists also learned that the content of dreams is influenced by age and gender. Children are more likely than adults to dream of animals and the animals they dream of are more likely to be large, threatening wildlife. On the contrary, university students usually dream of meiofauna, pets and domesticated animals. This may be because children feel that they control their own world much less than adults, so when they sleep, they see the world portrayed as a more horrific picture (Van de Castle, 1983, 1994).

p111.original: 相较于盎格鲁血统的美国大学生，墨西哥籍美国大学生的梦里更常出现与死亡相关的画面。这可能是因为死亡是墨西哥文化中较为突出的一部分，我们可以从其死亡纪念日所使用的图片中看出这一点。
p111.en: Mexican American university students' dreams are more frequent in death than in Anglo-American students. This may be because death is a more prominent part of Mexican culture, as we can see from the pictures used on the anniversary of death.

p112.original: 世界各地的女性都会经常梦到孩子，而男性则会经常梦到侵略、武器和工具（Murray，1995）。并且，美国女性比她们的男性同伴更可能成为公平的做梦者：在梦的研究人员卡尔文·霍尔（Calvin Hall）收集的超过1800个梦的样本中，女性会同时梦到男性和女性，而男性梦到男性的频率是他们梦到女性的两倍。霍尔还发现，梦中角色之间敌对的关系要远多于友好的往来，并且三分之二的情绪性的梦都具有消极情绪的性质，如愤怒和悲伤。
p112.en: Women around the world often dream about children, while men often dream about aggression, weapons and tools (Murray, 1995). Moreover, women in the United States are more likely than their male counterparts to be fair dreamers: of over 1800 dream samples collected by dream researchers Calvin Hall, women dream of both men and women, while men dream of men twice as often as they dream of women. Hall also found that the hostile relationship between the actors in the dream was far more hostile than friendly interaction, and that two thirds of the emotional dreams were of a negative emotional nature, such as anger and grief.

p113.original: 梦与最近的经历 梦的内容往往与我们最近的经历以及在前一天所想的事情相关。但奇怪的是，如果你故意不去想某件事情，那么它更可能会突然出现在你的梦里（Wegner et al.，2004）。因此，如果你整天都在担心你的工作，或者想要忘记它，你今晚就很有可能会做有关工作的梦，特别是在你第一个快速眼动睡眠期间。
p113.en: Dreams and recent experiences, the content of dreams are often related to our recent experiences and to what we thought the day before. But strangely, if you deliberately don't think about something, it's more likely that it suddenly appears in your dream (Wegner et al., 2004). So if you've been worried about your work all day or want to forget it, you're probably gonna have a dream about your work tonight, especially during your first quick eye contact.

p114.original: 因此，一般晚上的第一个梦会与前一天的事情相关。在第二个快速眼动睡眠期间（90分钟后）的梦常常建立在第一个快速眼动睡眠期间出现的梦的主题上。整个晚上都是这样，就像一个不断演变的谣言从一个人传给另一个人：尽管最后出现的梦可能和前一天的事情有联系，但这种联系已经很遥远了。因为晚上的最后一个梦是最有可能被记住的，所以我们可能意识不到其与前一天所发生的事的联系（Cartwright，1977；Kiester，1980）。
p114.en: So, the first dream of a normal evening is connected to the day before. Dreams during the second fast eye sleep (90 minutes later) are often based on the theme of the first fast eye sleep. This was the case all night, as an evolving rumour passed from one person to another: although the last dream might have been linked to the day before, it was far away. Because the last dream at night is most likely to be remembered, we may not be aware of its connection to what happened the previous day (Cartwright, 1977); Kiester, 1980.

p116.original: 既然我们已知道了人们会梦到什么类型的事情，现在，让我们研究一下做梦的目的是什么。进化心理学家提出，梦可能为我们提供了安全的机会来演练处理危险情况的方法，但相关证据尚不明确（Franklin & Zyphur，2005）。有些认知心理学家认为，梦是有意义的心理事件，反映了做梦者心理世界中重要的事项或幻想。另一些认知科学家正在寻找梦和记忆的关系，甚至提出，梦能够帮助我们在生活中进行意义构建（Stickgold，2011）。但是也有人认为，梦根本没有任何意义，仅仅是睡眠时大脑的随机活动。让我们看一下各方在有关梦的意义的讨论中的立场。
p116.en: Now that we know what kind of things people dream about, let's look at what the purpose of dreaming is. Evolutionary psychologists have suggested that dreams may provide us with a safe opportunity to rehearse approaches to dangerous situations, but the evidence is not clear (Franklin & Zypur, 2005). Some cognitive psychologists believe that dreams are meaningful psychological events that reflect important events or illusions in the mental world of the dreamer. Other cognitive scientists are looking for a relationship between dreams and memories, even suggesting that dreams can help us build meaning in our lives (Stickgold, 2011). But there are also those who believe that dreams have no meaning at all, just the random activity of the brain during sleep. Let us look at the positions of the parties in the discussions on the meaning of the dream.

p118.original: 在古代，以色列人把梦解释为来自上帝的信息。
p118.en: In ancient times, Israelis interpreted dreams as messages from God.

p119.original: 与他们同时代的埃及人试图通过睡在供奉梦之神塞拉皮斯的神庙里来影响梦。
p119.en: The Egyptians who were with them tried to influence their dreams by sleeping in the temple of Serapis, the god of dreams.

p120.original: 在印度，《吠陀经》描述了梦的宗教意义。
p120.en: In India, the Vedda scripture describes the religious significance of dreams.

p121.original: 在中国，做梦带有一些冒险的元素。
p121.en: In China, dreams carry some risk-taking elements.

p122.original: 古代中国人相信，做梦期间灵魂会在身体外游荡。因此，他们不愿意匆忙唤醒沉睡的人，免得灵魂找不到回身体的路（Dement，1980）。
p122.en: The ancient Chinese believe that the soul wanders outside the body during a dream. Therefore, they do not want to rush to awaken the sleeper so that the soul does not find its way back to its body (Dement, 1980).

p123.original: 从许多非洲和美洲原住民文化的角度来看，梦是清醒现实的延伸。因此，当传统的切罗基印第安人梦见被蛇咬伤时，他们会在醒来时接受适当的紧急治疗。同样，当一个非洲部落首领梦见英国时，他会订购一套英国服装；当他穿着新服装出现时，他的朋友们会祝贺他完成了这次旅行（Dement，1980）。
p123.en: From the perspective of many African and Native American cultures, dreams are a sobering extension of reality. Thus, when the traditional Cherokee Indians dream of being bitten by a snake, they wake up and receive appropriate emergency treatment. Similarly, when an African tribal leader dreamt of Britain, he ordered a set of British clothing; When he appeared in new clothes, his friends would congratulate him on completing his trip (Dement, 1980).

p124.original: 与这些民间观点不同，睡眠科学家以这样一个问题来走近梦：梦具有哪些生物学功能？最近，研究人员一直在关注梦的认知功能。
p124.en: Unlike these folk views, sleep scientists have come close to the question: what are the biological functions of dreams? Recently, researchers have been focusing on the cognitive function of dreams.

p125.original: 梦与记忆 关于梦，一些最令人兴奋的研究来自认知神经科学。例如，我们现在知道，快速眼动睡眠能帮助我们巩固记忆。当学生们学习一个困难的逻辑游戏时，那些享受了整晚快速眼动睡眠的人比那些在学习后被剥夺了快速眼动睡眠的人在第二天的任务中表现得更好（Smith，2004）。睡眠研究人员詹姆斯·马斯（James Maas）指出，事实上，在快速眼动睡眠期间，大脑会补充记忆网络中的神经递质。快速眼动睡眠可能有助于将新的经验编织到旧的记忆结构中（Greer，2004b）。
p125.en: Dreams and memories about dreams, some of the most exciting studies come from cognitive neuroscience. For example, we now know that fast eye contact sleep can help us to consolidate our memory. When students learn a difficult logical game, those who enjoy a full night's fast eye sleep perform better than those who are deprived of fast eye sleep after learning in the mission of the next day (Smith, 2004). The sleep researcher James Maas pointed out that, in fact, during rapid eye motion sleep, the brain supplements neurotransmitters in memory networks. Rapid eye-sleep may help to woven new experiences into old memory structures (Greer, 2004b).

p126.original: 近期的研究表明，非快速眼动睡眠也会选择性地增强某些类型的记忆，尤其是对事实和位置的记忆（Miller，2007）。在哈佛睡眠科学家鲍勃·斯蒂克戈尔德（Bob Stickgold）的实验室里，一组学生在电脑上花一小时来解决一个复杂的三维迷宫问题，期间会反复地在迷宫中的新位置重新开始。他们的目标之一是找到并记住迷宫中一棵树的位置。接下来，一半学生小睡了一会儿，另一半学生则从事安静的活动。小睡者被从非快速眼动睡眠中唤醒，并要求报告他们的梦。没有小睡的人在相同的时间间隔里回答他们思考的问题。后来，当学生再次解决迷宫问题时，梦到迷宫的小睡者会比研究中的其他学生更快地找到这棵树（Bower，2010）。
p126.en: Recent studies have shown that non-fast eye contact sleep can also selectively enhance certain types of memory, especially of facts and locations (Miller, 2007). In the laboratory of the Harvard sleep scientist Bob Stickgold, a group of students spent an hour on computers to solve a complex three-dimensional maze problem, during which time new positions in the maze were repeated. One of their objectives was to find and remember the location of a tree in the maze. Then, half of the students slept for a while, while the other half were engaged in quiet activities. Sleepers are awakened from sleep that is not moving fast and are asked to report their dreams. People without a nap answer their questions at the same time. Later, when students once again solve the maze problem, sleepers who dream of the maze find the tree faster than other students in the study (Bower, 2010).

p127.original: 梦是我们无意识的线索 与认知科学家用实验来研究梦的作用不同，一些心理学家（特别是精神分析学家）把梦归于西格蒙德·弗洛伊德提出的梦的理论。20世纪初，弗洛伊德提出了有史以来最复杂、最全面的梦及其意义的理论。尽管这一理论缺乏科学证据，但它仍产生了巨大的影响（Squier & Domhoff，1998）。在这一观点中，梦代表了“通往无意识的康庄大道”，由一个人隐藏的精神生活的线索所铺就。对弗洛伊德来说，对梦的分析成为精神分析的基石，正如在他的经典著作《梦的解析》（The Interpretation of Dreams，1900/2015）中所描述的那样。
p127.en: It's not the same thing that cognitive scientists use experiments to study dreams, and some psychologists (especially psychoanalysts) attribute them to the theory of Sigmund Freud's dream. At the beginning of the twentieth century, Freud presented the most complex and comprehensive dream ever and its meaning. Despite the lack of scientific evidence, this theory has had a significant impact (Squier & Domhoff, 1998). In this view, the dream represents “the path to the unwitting well-being”, laid by the clues of a person's hidden spiritual life. For Freud, the analysis of dreams became the cornerstone of the psychoanalysis, as described in his classic book The Analysis of Dreams, 1900/2015.

p128.original: 在精神分析理论中，梦有两个主要功能：
p128.en: In psychoanalytical theory, dreams have two main functions:

p129.original: 1. 守护睡眠（用符号伪装破坏性的想法）；
p129.en: 1. Protection of sleep (signal to disguise destructive ideas);

p130.en: 2. To serve as a source of aspiration.

p131.original: 弗洛伊德认为，梦通过缓解白天产生的精神紧张来扮演守护者的角色，并通过允许做梦者透过无意识欲望进行不会导致伤害的工作，来完成其实现愿望的作用。
p131.en: Freud believes that dreams play the role of guardian by easing the mental tension generated by day and by allowing dreamers to perform unharmed work through unconscious desires to fulfil their aspirations.

p132.original: 弗洛伊德对梦的显性内容（manifest content，梦的故事情节）和隐性内容（latent content，梦的象征意义）做出了重要的区分。因此，精神分析治疗师仔细检查他们的病人梦里的显性内容，寻找隐藏在潜意识中的动机和冲突的线索。例如，与性冲突有关的线索可能以长而硬的物体或容器的形式出现，在弗洛伊德的理论中，这些物体或容器象征着男性和女性的生殖器官。同样，一次离开或一次旅行可能代表死亡、损失或新起点。
p132.en: Freud made an important distinction between the visible content of dreams (manifest content, storyline of dreams) and the hidden content (latent content, symbolism of dreams). As a result, psychoanalyst therapists scrutinized the obvious content of their patients ' dreams and sought clues to hidden underlying motives and conflicts. For example, clues related to sexual conflict may appear in the form of long and hard objects or containers that, in Freudian theory, symbolize the reproductive organs of men and women. Similarly, a departure or a trip may represent a death, loss or new starting point.

p133.original: 你必须是一个受过训练的精神分析学家才能理解梦吗？不一定。在某些情况下，我们梦的显性内容与我们清醒时的生活有着很明显的联系。因此，象征意义只是稍作伪装。例如，一项研究发现，对离婚感到沮丧的人经常梦见过去的恋情（Cartwright，1984）。通过分析自己的梦的模式和内容，你也许能够解码自己梦中的许多形象和行为（Hall，1953/1966；Van de Castle，1994）。然而，我们必须强调，弗洛伊德对梦的隐性内容的解释几乎没有任何可靠的科学依据。
p133.en: Do you have to be a trained psychoanalyst to understand a dream? Not necessarily. In some cases, the explicit content of our dreams is clearly linked to our lives when we are sober. The symbolism, therefore, is only a slight disguise. For example, a study found that people frustrated with divorce often dream of past relationships (Cartwright, 1984). By analysing the patterns and content of your dreams, you may be able to decode many of the images and behaviours of your dreams (Hall, 1953/1966; Van de Castle, 1994. However, we must stress that Freud's interpretation of the hidden content of the dream has little or no solid scientific basis.

p134.original: 梦是大脑的随机活动 并不是每个人都相信梦的内容是有意义的，特别是激活合成理论（activation-synthesis theory）认为，当睡眠中的大脑试图为其自发产生的活动赋予意义时，就会产生梦（Leonard，1998；Squier & Domhoff，1998）。在这一观点中，梦起源于睡眠中脑干发出的周期性的神经放电。当这种能量扫过大脑皮层时，睡眠者会体验到感觉、记忆、动机、情绪和运动的印象（理论中的“激活”部分）。尽管大脑皮层的激活是随机的，它产生的形象可能在逻辑上没有联系，但是大脑试图对它所接收的刺激赋予意义。为了做到这一点，它编织了一个连贯的故事，把这些随机电脉冲中的“信息”放在了一起（理论中的“合成”部分）。因此，梦只不过是大脑从无意义的内容中寻找意义的一种方式。
p134.en: Dreams are random activities of the brain, not everyone believes in the content of a dream, especially when it activates the synthetic theory (activation-synthesis theory) that when the brain in sleep tries to give meaning to its spontaneous activities (Leonard, 1998); Squier & Domhoff, 1998. In this view, dreams arise from periodic neurodrain discharges from the brain stem in sleep. When this energy sweeps through the cortex of the brain, sleepers experience the impressions of feeling, memory, motivation, emotion and movement (the “activated” part of the theory). Although the activation of the cortex of the brain is random and the image it creates may be logically unconnected, the brain tries to give meaning to the stimulus it receives. In order to do so, it has woven a coherent story and put together the “information” in these random electrical impulses (the “synthesis” part of the theory). So dreams are just a way for the brain to look for meaning from meaningless content.

p135.original: 梦的显性内容和隐性内容之间的关系好比对艺术的诠释，例如，萨尔瓦多·达利（Salvador Dali）的《记忆的永恒》（Persistence of Memory）。在这里，柔软变形的时钟和其他超现实的图像代表了显性内容，而你对达利的画的意义的解释则是其隐性内容。
p135.en: The relationship between the explicit content of a dream and the hidden content is akin to the interpretation of art, for example, Salvador Dali, Persistence of Memory. Here, softly deformed clocks and other super-realistic images represent the obvious, and your explanation of the meaning of Dali's painting is its hidden content.

p136.original: 这一理论的最初支持者是J.艾伦·霍布森（J. Allan Hobson）和罗伯特·麦卡利（Robert McCarley），他们的观点基于这样的想法：大脑需要不断的刺激才能生长和发育（Hobson & McCarley，1977）。在睡眠中，大脑会阻断外界的刺激，所以快速眼动睡眠会出现，以提供来自内部的刺激。因此，梦的内容来自大脑的激活，而不是来自无意识的愿望或其他有意义的心理过程。尽管霍布森（Hobson，1988，2002）还声称，我们梦中的故事情节是被添加的“事后头脑风暴”，但他也确实承认，一个做梦者独特的激活合成可能仍然有一定的心理意义，它依赖于文化、性别、个性因素和近期所发生的事件的影响。
p136.en: The original supporters of this theory were J. Allan Hobson and Robert McCalley, based on the idea that the brain needed constant stimulation to grow and develop (Hobson & McCalley, 1977). In sleep, the brain stops the outside stimulation, so rapid eye motion sleep occurs to provide internal stimulation. The content of the dream is therefore derived from brain activation, not from unconscious desires or other meaningful psychological processes. Although Hobson, 1988, 2002 also claimed that the story of our dream was added to the “afterthoughtstorm”, he did admit that the unique activating synthesis of a dreamer might still have some psychological significance, depending on culture, gender, personality factors and the effects of recent events.

p137.original: 梦是创造性见解的源泉 即使霍布森和麦卡利是对的，即梦除了表明大脑试图从无意义内容中找到意义之外没有什么特别的意义，梦仍然可以成为创造性想法的源泉。事实上，如果我们没有从夜晚如此狂野但有时又很美妙的场景中获得灵感，那才是令人难以置信的。正如我们所看到的那样，作家、作曲家和科学家都已经这么做了。
p137.en: Dreams are the source of creative ideas, even though Hobson and McCalli are right, that is, dreams have no special meaning, except to show that the brain is trying to find meaning from meaningless content, and they can still be the source of creative ideas. In fact, it would be incredible if we did not get inspiration from a scene so wild at night, but sometimes wonderful. As we have seen, writers, composers and scientists have done so.

p138.original: “梦境探险家”罗伯特·莫斯（Robert Moss，1996）引用19世纪的生理学家赫尔曼·冯·赫尔姆霍兹（Herman von Helmholtz）的话，坚持认为做以下三件事可引起创造性的梦。
p138.en: Robert Moss, the Dream Explorer, quoted Herman von Helmholtz, the nineteenth-century physiologist, as insisting that three things could give rise to creative dreams.

p139.original: 1. 让自己沉浸在自己感兴趣的问题或议题中。
p139.en: 1. Put yourself in the hands of issues or issues of interest to itself.

p140.original: 2. 通过把注意力转移到轻松无关的事情上，让你的创造性想法得以酝酿。
p140.en: 2. By turning your attention to easy and irrelevant matters, your creative ideas can be developed.

p141.original: 3. 给自己时间去得到启示，突然灵光一闪，找到你所寻求的答案。
p141.en: Give yourself time to be inspired, and suddenly the light will shine and find the answer you seek.

p142.original: 在21世纪，对这一观点的实证支持正在积累。在快速眼动睡眠期间，我们的大脑似乎已经准备好用以前没有想到的方式将想法组合在一起了。当人们从快速眼动睡眠中醒来并完成单词联想任务时，他们会产生比清醒时更多的新鲜、奇异的联想。而且，对于学习复杂数学问题的学生，一整晚的睡眠会使他们找到解决问题的新方法的机会翻倍（Stickgold & Walker，2004）。仿佛我们正在进行快速眼动睡眠的大脑从我们清醒时的感受域中拓展出来，并利用这个机会尝试将想法进行新的组合，而这正是创造力的基础。
p142.en: In the twenty-first century, empirical support for this view is building up. During fast eye contact sleep, our brains seem ready to combine ideas in ways that were not previously thought out. When people wake up from fast-moving eyes and finish their hyenas, they produce more fresh and strange connections than when they wake up. Moreover, for students who study complex mathematics issues, overnight sleep doubles their chances of finding new solutions to problems (Stickgold & Walker, 2004). It's like we're trying to move our brain from our senses when we're awake, and we're trying to use this opportunity to try to make a new combination of ideas, which is the basis of creativity.

p143.original: 在下面的“试一试”版块中，尝试在梦中找到自己的创作灵感。
p143.en: In the section below, try to find your own creative inspiration in the dream.

p144.original: 试一试 在梦中寻找你的创作灵感
p144.en: Try and find your creative inspiration in your dreams.

p145.original: 1831年，瑞士一个阴雨绵绵的夏日，三位作家齐聚一堂，急切地互相挑战编鬼故事。然而，经过几天毫无灵感的努力，玛丽·沃尔斯顿·雪莱（Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley）很担心自己会空手而归。后来有一天晚上，随着这个问题在她的脑海中反复出现，她睡着了，过了一段时间醒来后，她的脑海里浮现出梦中那可怕的形象。她后来清楚地回忆起它们：
p145.en: In 1831, three writers gathered in Switzerland on a rainy summer, eagerly challenging each other to write ghost stories. However, after a few days of uninspiring efforts, Mary Wolstonecraft Shelley was worried that she would return empty-handed. Later, one night, as the issue had been repeated in her mind, she fell asleep and, after a while of waking up, the terrible image of the dream appeared in her mind. She then clearly recalled them:

p146.original: 我的想象不请自来，如鬼怪附体般地引导着我……我看见一个面色苍白的学生，跪在他创造的东西的旁边，在亵渎圣洁的艺术。我看到一个面目狰狞的男人的幻象逐渐延伸出来，然后……表现出生命的迹象，以一种令人不安的、半死不活的动作动弹着……即使是“造物主”，也会惊恐万分地从他那令人作呕的作品边马上跑开。
p146.en: My imagination came upon me like a ghost I saw a pale student kneeling next to what he had created, desecrating the art of sanctity. I see the illusions of a man who looks like a man gradually spread, and then I show the signs of life, moving in a disturbing, half-dead movement and even the "maker" would be terrified to run away from his disgusting work.

p147.original: 第二天一早，她写下了这样一句话：“那是在十一月的一个沉闷的夜晚……”就这样开始了她的“鬼故事”《弗兰肯斯坦》（Frankenstein）或《现代普罗米修斯》（The Modern Prometheus）的初稿。
p147.en: The following morning, she wrote a sentence saying, "It was a dreary night in November..." and so began her "ghost story" (Frankenstein) or "The Modern Prometheus."

p148.original: 你有没有想过你的梦可以成为你创作灵感的源泉？如果有，请尝试一下梦的研究人员罗伯特·莫斯提出的这个策略。
p148.en: Have you ever thought that your dreams could be a source of inspiration for you? If so, please try this strategy put forward by the dreamer Robert Moss.

p149.original: 让自己想一位在你所从事的领域中令你敬佩的专家。
p149.en: Let yourself think of an expert who you admire in your field of work.

p150.original: 在你睡觉之前，想象你正在向这个人寻求帮助来解决你的问题；然后告诉自己去梦中寻找答案。
p150.en: Before you go to bed, imagine you're looking for help from this man to solve your problems; And then tell yourself to go to the dream and find the answer.

p151.original: 当你醒来时，快速写下或简要描述出所有你能回忆起的有关你梦到的内容。如果你什么都记不起来，那么就写下任何你所想到的内容。
p151.en: When you wake up, write down or describe briefly all the things that you can remember about your dreams. If you can't remember anything, write anything you think of.

p152.original: 找一个可以分享你的梦的朋友，让朋友倾听并提供非评判性的反馈，帮助你找出梦中的意义和形象的新见解。
p152.en: Find a friend who can share your dreams, let friends listen and provide non-judgmental feedback, and help you find new ideas about the meaning and image of your dreams.

p153.original: 之后，当你重温你的笔记时，你可能会发现你对解决问题的方法“有了明显的倾向”（Moss，1996）。你后来对梦中想法的解释，可能会让你感到惊讶，因为你甚至不知道自己会在梦里得到启示。也许，如果你能创造性地控制你的梦，你就能创作出自己的小说，就像玛丽·沃尔斯·雪莱创作出《弗兰肯斯坦》那样。
p153.en: And then, when you revisit your notes, you may find that you have a clear tendency to solve the problem (Moss, 1996). Your subsequent interpretation of the idea in the dream may surprise you, because you don't even know you'll be inspired in the dream. Perhaps if you can control your dreams creatively, you can create your own novels, like Mary Walls Shelley made Frankenstein.

p154.original: 心理学很有用 睡眠障碍

p155.original: 有一亿多的美国人睡眠不足或睡眠质量差，你有这些问题吗？这些睡眠问题中有些与工作有关。例如，在上夜班的人中，超过一半的人每周至少打一次瞌睡！世界上一些最严重的事故（包括三里岛核电站和切尔诺贝利核电站的灾难性的辐射泄漏以及博帕尔核电站的大规模有毒化学物质的泄漏）都发生在深夜工人可能习惯于睡觉时，这绝非巧合。睡眠专家断言，许多事故的发生是因为关键人员由于睡眠不足而无法以最佳状态行使职责，正如我们在2010年印度坠机事件（Dement & Vaughan，1999）中所指出的那样。
p155.en: Do you have problems with over 100 million Americans suffering from sleep deficiencies or poor sleep quality? Some of these sleep problems are work-related. For example, more than half of those who work at night do slumber at least once a week! It is no coincidence that some of the world's worst accidents, including the catastrophic radiation leaks from the Tri-island and Chernobyl nuclear power plants and the massive toxic chemical spills from the Bhopal nuclear power plants, occurred at night when workers might be used to sleeping. Sleep experts assert that many accidents occur because key personnel are unable to perform their duties in the best possible state because of lack of sleep, as we pointed out in the 2010 Indian crash (Dement & Vaughan, 1999).

p156.original: 除了这些与工作有关的睡眠问题，睡眠研究人员的实验室还研究了几种临床上的睡眠障碍。有的很常见，有的既罕见又奇葩。有些是相对温和的，有些则可能危及生命。将它们联系在一起的一个要素是正常睡眠周期的一个或多个部分的紊乱。
p156.en: In addition to these work-related sleep problems, several clinical sleep disorders have been studied in the laboratories of sleep researchers. Some are common, some are rare and strange. Some are relatively moderate, while others may endanger life. An element that links them is the disorder of one or more parts of the normal sleep cycle.

p157.original: 失眠（insomnia）通常是当人们对自己的睡眠量感到不满意时的诊断。其症状包括长期无法快速入睡、在睡眠中频繁醒来或者在凌晨醒来。失眠症患者约占所有成年人人数的三分之一，这使其成为最常见的睡眠障碍（Dement & Vaughan，1999）。
p157.en: Insomnia is usually diagnosed when people are not satisfied with their sleep volume. Symptoms include prolonged inability to sleep quickly, frequent awakening in sleep or waking up in the morning. Insomnia accounts for about one third of all adults, making it the most common sleep disorder (Dement & Vaughan, 1999).

p158.original: 不过，偶尔失眠是正常的，尤其是当你的头脑里有令人兴奋或担忧的事情时。请不要担心：除非你尝试用巴比妥类药物或非处方“安眠药”来处理这个问题，否则这些事件不会带来特别的危害。这些药物会通过缩短快速眼动睡眠周期来扰乱正常的睡眠周期。因此，它们实际上会加重失眠的影响，会使用药者感到休息不足、更加困倦。新一代治疗失眠症的处方药（你在电视上看到过大量的广告）似乎避免了许多此类问题，尽管长期使用的研究仍在进行中（Harder，2005）。而失眠反弹和早晨的昏睡等副作用仍然困扰着一些用药者。还有一种方法是采用认知行为疗法进行心理治疗，它在帮助人们学习避免失眠的有效策略方面取得了明显的成效（Smith，2001）。
p158.en: However, occasional insomnia is normal, especially when there are exciting or worrying things in your head. Do not worry: these incidents will not pose a particular hazard unless you try to deal with the problem with barbituroids or non-prescribed “sleeping pills”. These drugs disrupt normal sleep cycles by shortening fast-action sleep cycles. As a result, they can actually exacerbate the insomnia effect, and they can be used by people who feel less rest and more tired. A new generation of prescription drugs for insomnia (a large number of advertisements you have seen on television) seems to have avoided many of these problems, although long-standing research is still under way (Harder, 2005). Side effects such as insomnia and morning sleep continue to plague some drug users. Another approach is the use of cognitive behaviour therapy for psychotherapy, which has had notable results in helping people learn effective strategies to avoid insomnia (Smith, 2001).

p159.original: 怎样才能避免失眠？你怎么认为？
p159.en: How can insomnia be avoided? What do you think?

p160.original: 你可以用多种方法来操控自己所处的环境，以便在夜里获得良好的睡眠。请考虑下面这些方法。
p160.en: You can manipulate your environment in a variety of ways to get a good night's sleep. Please consider the following approaches.

p161.original: 试着每天在相同的时间睡觉和起床。这有助于训练你的生物钟让你在可以睡觉的时候睡觉。
p161.en: Try sleeping and getting up at the same time every day. It helps to train your biological clocks so you can sleep while you can.

p162.original: 在你上床前把头脑中的烦恼清除掉。如果你在这方面有困难，可创建一本“忧虑日记”，你可以在睡觉前用它记下你的想法。合上本子，把它放到一边，提醒你自己，在一夜良好的睡眠后你可以更有效地处理所有的事情。
p162.en: Clear your mind before you go to bed. If you have difficulties in that regard, you can create a “earth diary”, which you can use to write down your thoughts before you go to bed. Close the book, put it aside, remind yourself that after a good night's sleep, you can handle everything more effectively.

p163.original: 保持一个令人放松的睡眠环境。尽量避免在卧室进行争论或其他促使大脑活跃的活动。相反，要创造一个让你感到平静和安全的睡眠环境。借助经典条件反射，这将帮助你的身体将你的睡眠区域与放松联系起来，从而促进良好的睡眠。
p163.en: Keep a relaxing sleep environment. To the extent possible, to avoid disputes in the bedroom or any other activity that may motivate the brain. Instead, create a peaceful and safe sleep environment. With classic reflections, it will help your body to link your sleep area to relaxation, thereby promoting good sleep.

p164.original: 培养帮助你放松的睡前习惯。例如，泡个热水澡或淋浴、冥想，或者听音乐来帮助你放松。
p164.en: Cultivate a bedtime habit that helps you relax. For example, take a hot bath or shower, meditation, or listen to music to help you relax.

p165.original: 保持你的睡眠环境黑暗。光亮会让我们的身体清醒。
p165.en: Keep your sleep dark. The light will keep our bodies awake.

p166.original: 避免上床前看电视、在计算机或其他电子屏幕上工作。屏幕发出的蓝光会诱使你的大脑认为现在仍然是白天。睡前一小时关掉电子屏幕，同时调暗家里的灯，这将帮助你的大脑产生褪黑激素，从而帮助你入睡。
p166.en: You don't watch TV before you go to bed, work on computers or other electronic screens. The blue light that comes out of the screen induces your brain to think it's still daylight. Turning off the electronic screen an hour before you go to sleep, and dimming the lights in your home, will help your brain to produce the black hormonal, and help you sleep.

p167.original: 避免上床前暴饮暴食和过量饮酒，二者都会破坏你的自然睡眠周期。
p167.en: And avoiding the rush to bed and the overdrinking of alcohol will destroy your natural sleep cycle.

p168.original: 有规律地锻炼，并在一天的早些时候锻炼。睡前几小时的剧烈的体育运动会抑制你快速入睡的能力。
p168.en: Exercised regularly and earlier in the day. A few hours of intense sports before sleep will inhibit your ability to sleep quickly.

p170.original: 另一种常见的疾病——睡眠呼吸暂停综合征（sleep apnea），常常不会被注意到，仅表现为白天嗜睡和睡眠同伴对其打鼾的抱怨。但在这类表现的背后，其真正原因是呼吸的异常。一个患有睡眠呼吸暂停综合征的人，会出现长达一分钟的呼吸暂停，每晚常常几百次（请不要担心，在夜间每小时短暂停止几次呼吸是正常的）。通常，这是由于睡眠者的肌张力放松导致喉咙里的气道塌陷。结果形成了睡眠呼吸暂停的第二个主要症状：频繁地大声打鼾。患者每次缺氧并试图通过塌陷的气道获得空气时都会发出鼾声（Seligson，1994）。当呼吸停止，睡眠者的血氧水平骤降时，身体的应急系统就会启动，导致应激激素在身体中流动。在此过程中，睡眠者会短暂醒来，再次开始呼吸，然后又睡着。因为这种情况大多发生在深度睡眠中，患者通常对这段经历没有记忆。
p170.en: Another common disease - sleep-respiration syndrome (sleep apnea) - is often invisible, as evidenced by the snoring complaints of sleep addiction and sleep peers during the day. But behind these manifestations, the real reason is respiratory abnormalities. A person suffering from a sleep-respiratory suspension syndrome is subject to a one-minute suspension of breathing, often hundreds of times every night (don't worry that it is normal to stop breathing several times at night). Usually, this is due to the breakdown of the gas tunnel in the throat as a result of sleeper's relaxing muscle tension. As a result, a second major symptom of sleep breathing pauses: frequent snoring with loud voice. Every time a patient lacks oxygen and attempts to obtain air through a collapsed airway, he snores (Seligson, 1994). When breath stops and the blood oxygen levels of sleepers drop sharply, the body emergency system is activated, resulting in the flow of stress hormones in the body. In the process, sleepers will wake up briefly, start breathing again and fall asleep again. Because most of this happens in deep sleep, patients usually have no memory of the experience.

p171.original: 如果睡眠呼吸暂停的患者及其家人和同事没有认识到问题的本质，他们可能就会将其注意力不集中或犯困等白天不正常的行为解释为懒惰或疏忽。这可能不仅会破坏人际关系，而且睡眠呼吸暂停还会产生有害的生物效应，包括损伤脑细胞与使血压升高，而这会向血管和心脏施加达到危险水平的压力（Gami et al.，2005）。
p171.en: If patients who are sleeping in their breath do not realize the nature of the problem, and their families and colleagues, they may interpret their irregular behaviour during the day, such as being distracted or trapped, as being lazy or negligent. This may not only disrupt interpersonal relationships, but also have harmful biological effects, including brain cell damage and increased blood pressure, which can put pressure on blood vessels and the heart at a dangerous level (Gami et al., 2005).

p172.original: 早产儿偶尔会出现睡眠呼吸暂停发作，他们可能需要身体刺激才能重新开始呼吸。此外，让小孩趴在床上睡觉会加重睡眠呼吸暂停出现的概率（睡眠科学家强烈建议“仰卧睡眠”）。显然，这个问题可能是致命的，它是婴儿猝死综合征（Sudden Infant Death Syndrome，SIDS）的一个可能原因。“早产儿”睡觉时必须与呼吸监护仪保持连接，直到他们发育不完全的呼吸系统变得成熟。相反，对于患有睡眠呼吸暂停综合征的成年人来说，并不需要过于担心自己会永久性呼吸暂停。对他们来说，治疗的重点是减少每晚数百次发作的呼吸暂停。这通常要借助一种设备来实现，该设备可以将充足的空气泵入肺部，并在睡眠时使气道保持畅通。
p172.en: Premature babies occasionally experience sleep-respiration suspensions, which may require physical irritation in order to re-breath. In addition, keeping a child in bed increases the probability of suspension of sleep breathing (sleeping scientists strongly recommend “sleeping on the back”). Clearly, the problem may be fatal, and it is a possible cause of the sudden death syndrome (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome, SIDS). “Premature babies” must be connected to the respiratory monitor when they sleep until their underdeveloped respiratory system matures. On the contrary, for adults suffering from sleep-respiratory suspension syndrome, there is no need to worry too much that they will have permanent respiratory suspension. For them, the focus of treatment is to reduce the number of respiratory pauses that occur hundreds of times a night. This is usually done by means of a device that pumps sufficient air into the lungs and keeps the airways open during sleep.

p173.original: 夜惊（night terrors），主要发生在儿童身上，不会对健康造成威胁，尽管它可能会使人很痛苦。夜惊发作通常会表现为一个看起来吓坏了的孩子在尖叫，这个孩子实际上处于睡眠状态的第四阶段，很难醒来。最后惊醒时，孩子可能仍然会感到害怕，但却对什么样的心理事件导致夜惊没有具体的记忆。事实上，受其困扰的家庭成员可能会比孩子更难忘记这一经历。大多数经历过夜惊的孩子，通常到青春期就会自愈。
p173.en: Night terrors, mainly on children, do not pose a health threat, although they can cause great suffering. Night terror usually manifests itself in the screams of a child who appears to be terrified and who is actually in the fourth phase of his sleep and who is hard to wake up. When finally awakened, the child may still be afraid, but there is no specific memory of what psychological events lead to night terror. In fact, family members who are beset by this experience may be harder to forget than children. Most children who have experienced night terror usually recover by adolescence.

p174.original: 与各种各样的噩梦不同，夜惊发生在深度睡眠而非快速眼动睡眠期间。在这个方面而言，它们像梦游、说梦话和遗尿一样，都发生在第四阶段。所有这些情况似乎都有遗传的影响。它们本身并不构成危险，不过梦游者可能会不小心从窗户上爬出来，或者走入繁忙的街道，所以有必要采取一些预防措施（顺便说一句，叫醒梦游者是危险的，这一说法不是真的）。在大多数情况下，梦游和夜惊在成年后会减少或消失。但如果它们带来持久的慢性问题，那么这个人的症状应该由睡眠专家进行评估。遗尿通常可以通过一个简单的行为改变程序来改善，该程序使用一个带有内置警报的垫子，会在潮湿时发出警报。
p174.en: Unlike all kinds of nightmares, night terror occurs during deep sleep rather than fast eye contact. In this respect, they all occur in phase IV, like sleepwalking, talking in dreams and urine. All these situations seem to have genetic effects. They do not in themselves pose a risk, but sleepwalkers may accidentally climb out of windows or walk into busy streets, so some precautions are necessary (by the way, it is not true that waking up sleepwalkers is dangerous). In most cases, sleepwalking and night terror decrease or disappear after adulthood. But if they cause chronic and persistent problems, then the symptoms of the individual should be assessed by sleep specialists. The urine can usually be improved by a simple behavioural change process, which uses a mattress with an built-in alarm, which sends an alarm during damp.

p175.en: I'm having a sexual sleeping disorder.

p176.original: 发作性睡病（narcolepsy，也称嗜睡症）是最不寻常的睡眠障碍，它会导致人们白天突然睡眠发作，通常没有任何预兆。但这并不是普通的昏昏欲睡。这些睡眠发作是如此突然，以致发作性睡病患者会报告说在爬梯子时或在6米深的水下潜水时睡着了。发作性睡病发作之前患者也可能会突然失去对肌肉的控制，这种情况被称为猝倒。
p176.en: Sexual sleeping disorders (narcolepsy, also known as sleeping disorders) are the most unusual sleep disorders that can lead to sudden sleep outbreaks during the day, usually without any warning. But it's not just an ordinary sleepover. These sleep attacks are so sudden that those who have sleeping sexually report falling asleep while climbing the ladder or diving underwater at a depth of 6 metres. Patients may also suddenly lose control of their muscles before having a sexual sleeping disease, a situation that is called sudden fall.

p177.original: 奇怪的是，任何令人兴奋的事情都会引发发作性睡病发作。例如，这些患者常常报告说，他们在为一个笑话开怀大笑时睡着了，甚至在做爱时睡着了。显然，发作性睡病是危险的，还对亲密关系不太好。
p177.en: Strangely, anything exciting can cause a sleeping disease. For example, these patients often report that they fall asleep when laughing at a joke and even when they make love. Clearly, sleeping with sex is dangerous and not very good for intimate relationships.

p178.original: 把这些碎片拼凑起来，我们发现，发作性睡病是快速眼动睡眠障碍的一种（Marschall，2007）。具体来说，睡眠记录显示，发作性睡病患者的睡眠有一个不正常的快速眼动期；也就是说，发作性睡病患者在睡眠开始时进入快速眼动睡眠，而不是像平常那样等待90分钟才开始进行快速眼动睡眠。你可能已经猜到了，伴随的猝倒仅仅是快速眼动的睡眠性麻痹。
p178.en: By putting together these fragments, we find that sexually transmitted diseases are a form of rapid eye motion disorder (Marschall, 2007). Specifically, sleep records indicate that there is an abnormally rapid eye contact period for sleeping with sleeping patients; In other words, people with sexually transmitted sleeping disorders enter rapid eye contact at the beginning of their sleep, rather than waiting for the usual 90 minutes before they begin rapid eye contact. You may have guessed that the sudden fall was just a quick eye-motion sleep palsy.

p179.original: 针对有发作性睡病的动物的研究表明，这种疾病是由影响脑干中睡眠控制回路的一个遗传问题造成的。最近的研究表明，这是由于下丘脑产生的一种化学物质下视丘分泌素供应的减少造成的（Harder，2004；Marschall，2007）。到目前为止，这种疾病尚无法治愈，但某些药物可以减少睡眠发作和猝倒的频率。既然我们知道是生物学的原因，发作性睡病患者就不应再被送去接受心理治疗，去寻找那些曾经被认为是疾病基础的无意识冲突。
p179.en: Studies of animals with sleeping disorders indicate that the disease is caused by a genetic problem that affects sleep control circuits in the brain stem. Recent studies have shown that this is due to a decrease in the supply of sub-optic urogens from a chemical produced in the hypothalamus (Harder, 2004); Marshall, 2007. To date, the disease has not been curable, but certain drugs can reduce the frequency of sleeping conditions and sudden fallout. Since we know that it is biology, people who have sex with sleeping patients should no longer be sent to psychological care to look for unconscious conflicts that were once considered to be the basis of the disease.

p180.original: 那么，如果你怀疑自己有睡眠障碍，例如，慢性失眠、睡眠呼吸暂停综合征或发作性睡病，你该怎么办呢？你应该先找睡眠专家进行评估。许多医院都有睡眠障碍门诊，你的医生或临床心理医生可以给你推荐。
p180.en: So what do you do if you suspect that you have sleep disorders, such as chronic insomnia, sleep respiratory suspension or sexually transmitted diseases? You should get an expert on sleep first. Many hospitals have sleeping disorders clinics, which your doctor or clinical psychologist can recommend to you.
